# ASST (Strive, Inc.) — Technical Analysis Report
**Analysis date: 2026-10-02**

## Indicators Selected and Rationale

Eight complementary indicators were chosen to cover trend, momentum, volatility, and confirmation without redundancy:

- **close_50_sma / close_10_ema** — medium-term trend baseline plus a fast trigger for short-term momentum shifts.
- **macd / macdh** — trend momentum and its rate of change (histogram catches deceleration before the MACD line itself rolls).
- **rsi** — overbought/oversold momentum gauge.
- **boll_ub / boll_lb** — volatility-adjusted extremes for breakout vs. reversal context.
- **atr** — absolute volatility for stop sizing and position risk framing.

(200 SMA and VWMA were skipped: the 50 SMA already anchors trend, and the verified snapshot confirms 200 SMA at 15.52 — far below price — adding little incremental signal.)

## Price Action Overview

ASST staged an extraordinary rally over the look-back window. From a base around $11–13 in early-to-mid August, the stock broke out violently starting 2026-08-19 (close $14.73 on 7.6M shares, roughly triple typical volume) and ran almost vertically: $18.22 (08-21), $21.39 (08-25), $24.22 (08-31), $27.14 (09-04), $30.09 (09-18), peaking at an intraday high of $32.08 on 2026-10-02 before closing at $30.03. That is roughly a 145–170% gain from mid-August lows to the 10-02 intraday high.

Critically, the character of the move has changed: after 09-18, price stopped making sustained new highs and moved into a sideways churn between roughly $28.70 and $30.80. The last 10 sessions (09-22 through 10-02) show closes compressed between $28.99 and $30.33 — a consolidation/distribution zone after a parabolic leg.

## Indicator Detail (verified snapshot values)

- **Trend:** Close $30.03 sits ~43% above the 50 SMA ($20.99) and ~94% above the 200 SMA ($15.52). This is a deeply extended trend — bullish structure, but the gap to the 50 SMA means mean-reversion risk is extreme. The 10 EMA ($29.35) is the active short-term floor; price closed above it on 10-02 but only marginally, and the EMA's slope is flattening (29.20 → 29.35 over two days vs. ~0.3/day earlier in September).
- **MACD/momentum deceleration:** MACD line at 2.35 is still strongly positive but has been declining every session since its 09-14 peak near 3.68. The MACD histogram is negative (−0.40) and has been negative or near-zero since 09-22 — momentum stalled well before price did, a textbook bearish divergence relative to the 09-18→10-02 flat-to-higher price range. MACD (2.35) is below its signal line (2.75).
- **RSI:** 69.82 — just under the 70 overbought threshold, but telling: RSI peaked at 83.85 on 09-14 when price was ~$29, and has made lower highs (79.0 on 09-21, ~70 now) while price retested the highs. Bearish momentum divergence confirmed.
- **Bollinger Bands:** Price at $30.03 sits between the midline ($28.69) and upper band ($31.13), with the bands still wide — consistent with an uptrend losing thrust rather than a fresh breakout. The 10-02 session traded above the upper band intraday (high $32.08 vs. band $31.13) and was rejected back inside, closing near mid-range — a failed-breakout / exhaustion-style candle on elevated volume (11.3M vs. ~4–8M recent norm).
- **ATR:** 1.89 — roughly 6.3% of price daily true range. Volatility is elevated and creeping up (1.63 on 09-02 → 1.89 now), which cuts both ways: continuation moves will be fast, but so will reversals. A 2×ATR stop sits ~$3.78 below entry, i.e., ~$26.25 — coincidentally near the lower Bollinger band.

## Actionable Insights

- **Bull case:** Structure remains firmly bullish — price above all major MAs, MACD deeply positive, and the post-09-18 range has held above the 10 EMA and prior $29 breakout shelf. A decisive close above $31.13 (upper band) with volume would signal the next leg; the 10-02 intraday push to $32.08 shows buyers still probe upside.
- **Bear case / caution:** Momentum has been deteriorating for ~3 weeks while price ground sideways — negative MACD histogram, declining RSI from 83.85 to 69.82, price ~43% over the 50 SMA, and a high-volume rejection at the band top on 10-02. A close below the 10 EMA ($29.35) and especially below the $28.69 midline / $28.30–28.70 shelf would open a fast mean-reversion toward $26.25 (lower band) and potentially the rising 50 SMA ($20.99) on a deeper unwind.
- **Risk framing:** At 6.3% daily ATR, position sizing should be materially reduced vs. normal-volatility names. Tight stops will be whipsawed; stops below $28.60–26.25 align with structure rather than noise.
- **Net read:** Strong trend, exhausted momentum. Favor patience: either a confirmed breakout above $31.10–32.10, or a pullback entry near $28.70/$26.25. Chasing at the upper band into a momentum divergence is the lowest-quality entry on the board.

## Key Points Summary

| Category | Signal | Evidence (verified) |
|---|---|---|
| Trend | Strongly bullish, extended | Close $30.03 vs 50 SMA $20.99 (+43%), 200 SMA $15.52 (+94%) |
| Short-term momentum | Stalling | Close barely above 10 EMA $29.35; flat closes $28.99–$30.33 since 09-22 |
| MACD | Bullish level, bearish direction | MACD 2.35 below signal 2.75; histogram −0.40; falling since 09-14 peak ~3.68 |
| RSI | Near-overbought, diverging | 69.82 now vs 83.85 on 09-14 at lower price — lower highs |
| Bollinger | Rejected at upper band | High $32.08 vs band $31.13 on 10-02, closed $30.03 |
| Volatility | Elevated, rising | ATR 1.89 (~6.3% of price), up from 1.63 on 09-02 |
| Key resistance | $31.13–$32.08 | Upper band + 10-02 intraday high |
| Key support | $29.35 / $28.69 / $26.25 | 10 EMA / Bollinger midline / lower band |
| Volume | High on rejection | 11.3M on 10-02 vs ~4–8M recent sessions |
| Overall bias | Bullish structure, tired momentum; wait for breakout or pullback rather than chasing | — |

### Yahoo Finance news — UNAVAILABLE
The news feed returned a placeholder for the entire window: Yahoo only serves recent items, so no institutional framing was captured. This is a tooling limitation, not confirmed silence — there may well be ASST news coverage this week that we cannot see. No weight can be assigned to this source.

This is the only working source. Labeled sentiment: **8 Bullish (28%) vs 1 Bearish (3%)**, with 20 unlabeled. The labeled split is 8:1 bullish — strongly positive, though on a small absolute count.

Notably, several of the "manipulation" complaints come from holders frustrated by price suppression — annoyance at market makers rather than a bearish thesis on the company. Net read: engaged, predominantly bullish retail crowd with elevated volatility awareness.

Cannot be assessed — two of three sources are placeholders. The entire report rests on one day's worth of StockTwits messages (all 29 are timestamped 2026-10-02), so even within the single source there is no time-depth across the analysis window.

1. **Bitcoin-treasury thesis**: ASST is discussed as a leveraged Bitcoin play — references to ~1,557 BTC added to the stack this week (+5.67%), BTC-linked portfolio allocations, and hopes pinned on Bitcoin reaching $500K by 2030. Sentiment is tightly coupled to BTC price action.

3. **Manipulation/volatility complaints**: Recurring claims of MM suppression and "blatant manipulation" alongside "wild volatility..love it" — high churn, active traders.
4. **MSTR comparison/spillover**: ASST is repeatedly framed against MSTR, with some users arguing ASST has better management, and one rotating the other way.

## 4. Catalysts and risks surfaced
- **Catalyst**: Warrant-trigger price zone (~33–35) ahead of the ~Oct 13 window the community is watching; continued weekly BTC accumulation announcements.
- **Risk**: Warrant-related dilution/selling pressure (one holder explicitly exited over it); heavy dependence on Bitcoin's price; retail chatter of "manipulation" indicates volatile, thin, momentum-driven trading; +125% over 90 days means the crowd may be leaning in late — contrarian caution applies if bullishness approaches extremes.

## 5. Key signal summary

| Labeled sentiment ratio | Bullish | StockTwits | 8 Bullish vs 1 Bearish (8:1) across 29 msgs |
| Bitcoin accumulation | Bullish | StockTwits | ~1,557 BTC added this week (+5.67%), cited approvingly |
| Warrant-trigger thesis | Bullish (conditional) | StockTwits | "run her up to 33-35"; patience until ~Oct 13 |
| Warrant dilution / exits | Bearish | StockTwits | holder moved position to $MSTR/$BMNR over warrant fears |
| Manipulation complaints | Mixed/noise | StockTwits | "blatant manipulation", "MMs slam it down" — frustration, not thesis |
| Institutional/news framing | Unknown | Yahoo Finance | Source unavailable — no data |
| Long-term investor discussion | Unknown | Reddit | Source unavailable — no data |

## Bottom line
Mildly Bullish. The one available source shows a clearly bullish retail skew (8:1 labeled ratio, constructive unlabeled majority) anchored on a Bitcoin-treasury narrative and a near-term warrant-trigger catalyst. Confidence is **low**: two of three sources are placeholders, the sample is 29 messages from a single day, and the bullish skew coexists with real warrant-dilution concerns and manipulation chatter typical of a volatile, speculative name. Treat this as a thin retail-sentiment snapshot for the trader to weigh, not a robust signal.

# ASST (Strive, Inc.) — Fundamentals Report
Point-in-time as of 2026-10-02. All figures from SEC EDGAR facts filed on or before that date, USD in millions unless noted.

## 1. Data Availability Caveats
- Profile-level fundamentals (market cap, valuation multiples, sector/industry, 52-week range) were withheld by the vendor to avoid look-ahead bias — only filed statements are available.
- Insider transactions were withheld: the vendor cannot establish which trades were public as of 2026-10-02.
- Cost of revenue / gross profit are not tagged by this filer, so margin structure cannot be computed from EDGAR facts.

## 2. Company Profile & Trajectory
ASST (Strive, Inc.) filed near-zero financials through 2023 — a shell-scale entity with total assets of ~$2–6M and negligible revenue. A dramatic transformation shows up in late 2025: total assets jumped to $793M (2025-09-30), then $746M (2025-12-31), $1.1B (2026-03-31), and $1.377B (2026-06-30). Stockholders' equity swung to $779M at 2025-09-30 (from -$4M immediately prior), consistent with a large capital raise / reverse-merger-style recapitalization — financing cash flow of +$943M in Q4 2025 and +$703M in H1 2026. The investing outflows (-$855M in Q4 2025, -$585M in H1 2026) alongside a huge cash balance suggest capital was deployed into a large asset position (consistent with a treasury-asset strategy, though the asset composition is not broken out in these facts).

## 3. Balance Sheet (quarterly)
- Total assets: $1,377M (2026-06-30), up from $28M one year earlier — a ~50x scale change.
- Cash & equivalents: $145M (2026-06-30), $95M (2026-03-31), $67M (2025-12-31).
- Current assets: $193M vs. total $1,377M → ~$1.18B of assets are non-current (the deployed capital).
- Liabilities remain tiny: $29M total ($25M current) at 2026-06-30 — essentially unlevered.
- Stockholders' equity: $646M (2026-06-30), down from $715M (Q1) and $779M (Sep 2025 peak) — equity is being eroded by operating losses and/or asset mark-downs.
- Book value fell ~17% from Sep 2025 peak to Jun 2026 despite continued capital raises → persistent value burn.

## 4. Income Statement (quarterly)
- Revenue is trivial relative to the balance sheet: $3M in each of Q1 and Q2 2026; TTM revenue ~$8–9M.
- Operating income: -$258M (Q2 2026), -$313M (Q1 2026), -$241M (Q4 2025). Losses are enormous relative to revenue — driven by expenses and/or unrealized losses on holdings flowing through operations.
- Net income: -$258M (Q2 2026), -$266M (Q1 2026), -$394M (Q4 2025). Cumulative net loss over the last three reported quarters ≈ -$918M — roughly two-thirds of peak equity.
- Diluted EPS: -$3.77 (Q2 2026), -$4.53 (Q1 2026), -$9.04 (Q4 2025). EPS losses are shrinking per share partly because the share count has exploded via financing.

## 5. Cash Flow
- Operating cash flow is consistently negative and worsening in absolute terms: -$39M in H1 2026, -$25M FY2025, -$18M for the 9 months to Sep 2025.
- Financing is the lifeline: +$943M (Q4 2025), +$182M (Q1 2026), +$703M (H1 2026). The company funds both its operating burn and its asset purchases entirely through issuance — classic dilution-financed model.
- Investing: -$855M (Q4 2025) and -$585M (H1 2026) — the raised capital is being deployed into non-current assets.
- Capex ≈ $0 — this is a financial-asset vehicle, not an operating business.

## 6. Key Insights for Traders
- This is not an operating company; it is a leveraged-to-nothing, equity-financed asset vehicle. Fair value tracks its holdings, not its $3M/quarter revenue.
- Solvency is not the risk (liabilities ~2% of assets); the risks are (a) mark-to-market swings in the ~$1.18B non-current asset position, (b) ongoing dilution to fund a ~$20M/quarter operating burn, and (c) NAV-per-share erosion.
- Equity declined from $779M → $646M over three quarters while ~$885M of new financing came in — underlying asset/operating losses exceeded fresh capital. Dilution is masking per-share deterioration.
- Diluted share count is expanding rapidly (EPS loss shrinking while absolute net loss stays ~$260M/quarter) — watch for continued equity issuance announcements.
- Net income volatility (-$14M → -$394M → -$266M → -$258M) implies large non-operating marks; quarter-to-quarter earnings will be dominated by asset repricing, not business momentum.
- Insider transaction data unavailable at this vintage — cannot assess insider sentiment.

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case for ASST (Strive, Inc.) — Opening Argument

Let me be direct: ASST isn't a traditional operating company, and I won't pretend it is. It's a Bitcoin-treasury vehicle — and judged on the right axis, the bull case is strong. Here's why.

## 1. The core thesis: leveraged Bitcoin exposure with an active accumulation engine

Strive has transformed from a shell-scale entity (~$2–6M in assets through 2023) into a ~$1.4B asset vehicle in under a year. That's not drift — that's a deliberate, aggressively executed treasury strategy. The community data confirms it's still accelerating: roughly **1,557 BTC added in a single week (+5.67% of the stack)**. This is a company doing exactly what the MSTR playbook proved works — raise capital, convert to scarce digital assets, compound per-share exposure — but earlier in its curve, where the growth rate is highest.

If you believe Bitcoin appreciates over the next 12–24 months — and the macro setup says it can — ASST is a higher-beta way to express that view than BTC itself.

## 2. The tape confirms it: +145–170% in six weeks, and the move isn't broken

From ~$11–13 in mid-August to a $32.08 intraday high on 10-02. Price sits 43% above the 50 SMA and 94% above the 200 SMA — yes, extended, but every major moving average is below price and rising. The post-09-18 range between ~$28.70 and $30.80 is **consolidation on top of a parabolic leg, not distribution**: it has held above the 10 EMA and above the prior $29 breakout shelf for ten straight sessions. Strong trends rest sideways, then resolve in the direction of the trend. That's what bases do.

And on 10-02, buyers probed $32.08 intraday — above the upper Bollinger band — on 11.3M shares, nearly double the recent norm. That's demand still knocking on the door of resistance, not exhaustion selling. A decisive close above $31.10–32.10 opens the next leg.

## 3. The macro tailwind is custom-built for this stock

This week's tape: weak jobs report → yields ease → "rate-hike expectations fade" → speculative growth and high-beta names rally. That is precisely the transmission channel that lifts a Bitcoin-treasury small-cap. Lower yields weaken the dollar-denominated hurdle for hard assets and put a bid under risk. ASST sits at the intersection of both: high-beta equity **and** a leveraged BTC proxy.

## 4. The retail bid is real — 8:1 bullish with a concrete catalyst

The one live sentiment source shows an **8:1 labeled bullish-to-bearish ratio** on StockTwits, and the unlabeled majority leans bullish too. More importantly, the crowd is organized around a specific near-term catalyst: **the warrant-trigger zone around $33–35 ahead of the ~October 13 window**. Bulls there aren't just hoping — they have a structural argument: running price into the exercise zone converts overhang into capital, which converts into more BTC on the balance sheet. That's a reflexive flywheel, the same dynamic that powered MSTR's premium-to-NAV for years.

## 5. Preempting the bear's best punches

I know what's coming, so let me take the arguments head-on:

**"It lost ~$918M over three quarters."** Those aren't operating losses — they're mark-to-market swings on a ~$1.2B asset position flowing through the income statement. A treasury vehicle's GAAP earnings are a function of when the asset was marked, not business health. Judge it on NAV and BTC-per-share trajectory, not EPS. Bears quoting -$3.77 EPS are applying an operating-company yardstick to an asset vehicle — category error.

**"Equity fell from $779M to $646M."** Correct — over a window that included deep drawdown marks. But the accumulation continued through it: financing inflows of $703M in H1 2026 funded both the burn and the stack. The operating burn is ~$20M/quarter against $145M cash — years of runway — and liabilities are a trivial $29M (2% of assets). There is no solvency risk here. Zero leverage means no forced-selling spiral, which is precisely what killed leveraged crypto vehicles in past cycles.

**"Dilution is exploding."** Dilution is the *business model*, not a defect — it's how the BTC stack grows. The question is whether issuance is accretive to BTC-per-share, and the weekly accumulation data says it is. Yes, the warrant overhang is real — but it's also the catalyst. Post-exercise, overhang becomes capital and the dilution fear trade unwinds.

**"Momentum divergence — RSI down from 83.85, MACD histogram negative."** Three weeks of sideways consolidation after +150% is healthy, not ominous. Divergences in strong trends resolve through time-correction, and this one has: price held the $28.69 midline and 10 EMA while indicators cooled off. That's exactly the reset that precedes continuation. The bear reads a staircase as a cliff.

**"Sentiment is thin, one source, 29 messages."** Fair — low confidence. But directionally it's 8:1 bullish with an engaged holder base and a dated catalyst. Thin data pointing one way beats no data.

## Bottom line

ASST is a ~$1.4B, unlevered, rapidly growing Bitcoin-treasury vehicle trading in a dovish-repricing tape that rewards exactly this kind of asset. The technical structure is a high-and-tight consolidation above every major average, with a live warrant catalyst at $33–35 and a retail base that's 8:1 bullish. The bear case amounts to "it's volatile and GAAP earnings look ugly" — true of every early-stage treasury vehicle, and precisely why the upside is still mispriced. The risk-managed play: the $28.69–29.35 zone is the floor; a break above $31.13–32.10 confirms the next leg. The structure says the path of least resistance is up.

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case Against ASST (Strive, Inc.) — Rebuttal to the Bull

Nice try, Bull. You gave a polished speech, but every pillar of it leans on a premise that collapses under its own weight. Let me take it apart piece by piece — then show you what the tape is actually saying.

## 1. "Dilution is the business model" is not a defense — it's the indictment

You conceded the most damning fact in the filing record while trying to wave it off. Between Sep 2025 and Jun 2026, ASST raised roughly **$885M in fresh financing** — and stockholders' equity still *fell* from $779M to $646M. Read that again: the company took in nearly nine hundred million new dollars and ended up with *less* equity than it started with. Underlying losses exceeded the entire capital intake. The "MSTR playbook" you cite works only if issuance is accretive — and your own accretion test fails. You claim "the weekly accumulation data says it is," but no data in this packet demonstrates BTC-per-share growth. We have an asset pile growing in gross terms and a share count "exploding" (the fundamentals report's word, not mine) in lockstep. EPS losses shrinking purely because the denominator grew is arithmetic, not value creation. A vehicle that must issue equity to survive an ~$80M/year operating burn while its marks bleed is not a flywheel — it's a treadmill, and the treadmill only runs while the stock price stays elevated enough to sell into. Which brings us to the reflexivity you're willfully ignoring: the entire model needs a high share price to issue accretively. The moment this premium collapses — and parabolic premiums always collapse — dilution turns punitive, the accumulation engine stalls, and the narrative feeding the premium dies with it. Reflexivity cuts both ways; you're only describing the up-stroke.

## 2. The mark-to-market defense cuts against you

"It's just marks, not operating losses" — exactly. You're telling me to ignore GAAP because a treasury vehicle's earnings are "a function of when the asset was marked." Agreed. And what that means is that a **-$258M quarter is a real impairment signal about the holdings themselves**, not accounting noise. The loss sequence — -$14M → -$394M → -$266M → -$258M — isn't shrinking meaningfully. You can't wave away $918M of cumulative marks over three quarters and simultaneously ask me to price the stock off NAV, because those marks *are* the NAV story. And if the assets were marked down that hard through H1 2026 while the stock then rallied 150%+ into October, the gap between price and any reasonable NAV estimate has blown out, not closed. You're effectively asking buyers at $30 to pay a momentum premium on top of assets that were already shrinking — and the vendor deliberately withheld market cap and multiples, which should tell you how uncomfortable the valuation math is.

## 3. The warrant "catalyst" is a sell wall wearing a costume

This is where the bull case gets genuinely dangerous. You describe the $33–35 warrant zone as a "reflexive flywheel" — run the price up, convert overhang into capital, buy more BTC. But read the sentiment report's own data: **very few warrants executed so far, holders cashing out before expiry**, and at least one holder explicitly rotated out of ASST into MSTR/BMNR *because of the warrant overhang*. What you call a catalyst is mechanically a supply event: a price zone where a large block of paper converts into shares that must be absorbed or sold. The "structural reason for a push higher" you cite is literally a coordinated squeeze narrative from a 29-message, single-day StockTwits sample — the same thread where users complain of "blatant manipulation" and ask "was this the top?" That's not an organized catalyst; that's a crowded room staring at the same exit door marked October 13. If price approaches $33–35, warrant holders sell into it. If it doesn't get there, the narrative the bid is built on expires worthless. Both paths resolve against the buyer at $30.

## 4. The technicals say distribution, and you admitted the evidence

You called my staircase a cliff. Let me return the favor: you're calling a three-week momentum collapse a "rest," and the data disagrees with you on every axis:

- **MACD has declined every single session since 09-14** — from ~3.68 to 2.35, now below its signal line, histogram negative since 09-22. That's not consolidation; that's sellers quietly working while price holds.
- **RSI diverged twice**: 83.85 → 79.0 → 69.82, lower highs on momentum while price retested the highs. Textbook.
- **The 10-02 candle was a rejection, not a probe**: ran to $32.08, *above* the upper band, and got sold back to $30.03 on 11.3M shares — nearly triple the 4–8M norm. High volume at the high that fails to hold is the definition of distribution. You read that as "demand knocking on the door." Who sells 11.3M shares into a breakout attempt if demand is in control? Someone with a lot of shares and a calendar — see point 3.
- Price is **43% above the 50 SMA and 94% above the 200 SMA** after a 150%+ parabolic leg. Your "high-and-tight flag" sits six weeks after a vertical move on a name with a 6.3% daily ATR. Mean-reversion targets are already on the board: $28.69 midline, $26.25 lower band — that's one bad session away — and on a real unwind, the rising 50 SMA at $20.99, ~30% below current price.

Bases in strong trends resolve upward when momentum *resets and rebuilds*. Here momentum kept bleeding for three straight weeks while churn volume stayed elevated. That's the fingerprint of distribution, not rest.

## 5. The macro tailwind is borrowed and one print deep

Your macro case is real but thin by your own report's admission: the entire risk-on impulse rests on **one weak jobs print**. A hot CPI or a hawkish speaker inverts it — and the report itself says regimes like this "reverse fast," hitting high-beta names hardest. You've strapped investors to a leveraged-BTC proxy whose BTC correlation is the *uncontrolled* variable in all of this: if Bitcoin chops or sells off into October 13, every other argument — the warrant zone, the momentum, the premium — unwinds simultaneously. Even the StockTwits crowd concedes a BTC rally *after* Oct 13 is "wasted." That's a binary date wrapped in a binary asset.

## 6. What this stock actually is

Strip the narrative and the filings describe a shell that became a $1.4B dilution-financed asset vehicle in under a year, burning ~$20M/quarter, with ~$3M/quarter of revenue, an exploding share count, an equity line shrinking despite massive raises, insider data withheld, no verified company news in the window, and sentiment resting on 29 messages from one day on one platform. Every data gap in this packet — withheld multiples, withheld insider transactions, unavailable news and Reddit feeds — sits on the bearish side of the ledger.

## Bottom line

The bull case is a bet that three things go right at once: Bitcoin cooperates, the $33–35 warrant zone converts to capital instead of a sell wall, and a parabolic stock resolves a three-week momentum divergence upward from 43% above its 50 SMA. The bear case needs only one of those to fail. The tape on 10-02 — a high-volume rejection at the upper band with a negative MACD histogram — says the smart money may already be distributing into the crowd that's 8:1 bullish. Downside map: $29.35 breaks, $28.69 goes quickly, $26.25 is the first real floor, and $21 is in play on a genuine unwind — against an upside case capped by a known supply zone at $33–35. That's asymmetry, all right — just not the direction you're selling.

**Position: Avoid/underweight.** Chasing here means buying a dilution-dependent vehicle at the top of a momentum divergence, two weeks before the exact supply event the bulls are calling a catalyst.
